Subject: Topology walkthrough request: private VPC anchors & control/data paths

Hi Karthik / Kimberly,

Thanks again for the demo last week. As we get into procurement, our network and security teams want a short walkthrough focused specifically on the "anchor" points you recommend for a private VPC deployment and how the control plane and data plane traffic traverse those anchors. Key asks from our side:

- Clear diagram of control-plane endpoints and expected egress destinations
- IP ranges / ports to allow for initial connectivity and subsequent updates
- How KV/prefix caching affects egress (are there callbacks to hosted endpoints?)
- Failover behavior if a regional anchor is degraded

Can we schedule a 45–60 minute session next week? I've attached our initial diagram (brightline_initial_diagram.vsdx) to give context.

Thanks,
Sarah Miller
Senior Cloud Architect
Brightline Health
S: +1 (415) 555-0123

Attachments: brightline_initial_diagram.vsdx

From: karthik_iyer@redwood.ai <karthik_iyer@redwood.ai>

Cc: kimberly_park@redwood.ai, irene_choi@redwood.ai, aditya_rao@redwood.ai
Date: Sat, 29 Aug 2026 10:02:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Topology walkthrough request: private VPC anchors & control/data paths

Hi Sarah — appreciate the clear asks. We can absolutely run a focused session. Proposed agenda below (45 mins):

1) Quick alignment (5m) — goals and success criteria
2) Control-plane anchors (10m) — management endpoints, auth, and IP/port expectations
3) Data-plane anchors (10m) — inference ingress, egress, caching, and regional failover
4) Ops/playbook (10m) — how to validate connectivity, what to monitor, runbook pointers
5) Q&A / next steps (10m)

Pre-reads: I'll share a short checklist (redwood_anchor_checklist.pdf) and a reference topology on the shared Drive: https://drive.redwood.com/shared/brightline/vpc-anchor-design.

Notes on what we'll cover so you can route to the right teams:
- Control plane is a customer-managed control-plane endpoint (we support a private control plane option) — connectivity is outbound TLS to a small set of managed IPs; we'll provide CIDR blocks during the call.
- Data plane (inference nodes) should be able to reach the anchor(s) over mTLS for registry and model artifact sync. For real-time inference, requests can be routed internally (no egress) if you host inference in the same VPC; otherwise, outbound for metrics/telemetry occurs to our telemetry aggregator.
- KV/prefix cache: cache priming is local to the inference hosts; however, cache misses can trigger small metadata calls to the control plane. We'll show expected call patterns and rates for your projected QPS.

Possible times (PT): Mon 9/31 10:00–11:00, Tue 9/1 14:00–15:00, Wed 9/2 09:00–10:00. Tell me which works and I'll send a calendar invite.

-karthik
Karthik Iyer
Staff Solutions Architect, Redwood Inference

Attachments: redwood_anchor_checklist.pdf

From: kimberly_park@redwood.ai <kimberly_park@redwood.ai>

Cc: irene_choi@redwood.ai, aditya_rao@redwood.ai, neha_kapoor@redwood.ai
Date: Sun, 30 Aug 2026 08:15:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Topology walkthrough request: private VPC anchors & control/data paths

Sarah / team — adding a few implementation notes ahead of the call so the security group/IP list is not surprising: 

- Control-plane outbound: expect TLS to three aggregator CIDRs (we'll provide exact /24s); ports: 443 and 5222 for internal control channel fallback.
- Data-plane artifact sync: mTLS on port 8443 to our artifact registry (we support SNI).
- Telemetry: metrics/alerts can be configured to flow to your internal telemetry collector; if you choose Redwood hosted telemetry, only outbound to our telemetry CIDR is required.
- KV cache behavior: most cache traffic is intra-node; metadata calls on cache poison will be <1% of token write throughput; if your environment has strict egress policies, we'll provide a mode that bundles metadata with the artifact sync window to reduce spiky egress.

One ops caveat: during rolling model reloads we may need short control-plane callbacks to retrieve new kernels; these are short-lived outbound fetches. We'll include them in the runbook.

If you can confirm whether your SC team requires explicit IP-by-IP allowlists vs. CIDR blocks, we can surface both in the call.

-kimberly
Kimberly Park
Director, Cloud Security 
Redwood Inference
